data.translation: <...> Then enmity arose between us; at Mart Shmuni they fought with us, six of them, and struck our young men.

Printed ṣləfwolle is retained; reduced ṣləf- and final -lle favour a -wa plus L-series actor analysis, but the form needs confirmation and does not independently establish a full paradigm. English is the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation.

summary: All three tokens fit wounding. Active ṣləfle takes an affected head as object, while Detransitive ṣlif makes the affected head the subject and leaves the agent unexpressed.
The 115/35 active event and 115/45 retrospective account describe the same injury; they illustrate different form boxes, not independent lexical senses or two independent events.
The inherited Detransitive box has no numbered sense list. Explicit Detransitive 1 is supplied without changing the active sense or inherited wording.

PrS 83/15 is a near-verbatim repetition of the inherited stone/woman example. The current entry cites prs 240/24, while the reader claims prs 241/15; neither claim licenses a silent citation replacement.
ṣləfole in the stone passage is consistent with a masculine actor ending and a feminine patient. Whether the actor is the boy or the narration permits another analysis remains a question.
No new idiom is established.

Jan 2.4/493 has patient subjects with məṣləfiwo in a sequence of colliding and falling. This supports injury arising without an expressed external agent. The reciprocal phrase b ḥḏoḏe belongs to qayṯiwo, not a separately reciprocal government of ṣlf.

Jan 2.22/4013 contrasts six opponents as actor with l-marked lan naʕimayḏan as affected humans. ṣləfwolle is provisionally Preterit-wa, with final -lle plausibly an L-series actor rather than the object claimed by the reader. An Infectum-wa reading is not adopted without explaining the reduced base and final L ending.
The supplied English struck in Jan 2.22/4013 does not justify a new generic hitting sense. The lexical injury reading is retained, and no assumption about wound severity is added.
Reconcile supplied PrS 83/15 with inherited prs 240/24 and the reader's unsupported prs 241/15 before changing any citation.
PrS 83/15: confirm the agent segmentation of ṣləfole and whether the boy remains its agent.
Does inherited 115/166 refer to a parallel head injury? It cannot be verified from the three supplied occurrences and is retained.

Jan supports round-1 Detransitive 1 verwundet werden in an injury-after-collision/falling sequence; the new contribution is Infectum-wa, not a new Detransitive sense.
